title: Peritoneal dialysis

steps.tx: Rippe's **three-pore model** of peritoneal membrane permeability describes three distinct functional pore sizes: ultrasmall transcellular **aquaporin-1** pores (radius < **0.5** nm, mediating water-only transport without solute), small interendothelial pores (radius **4** to **5** nm, mediating small-solute diffusion), and large venular pores (radius > **20** nm, mediating macromolecular protein leak).
steps.say: Rippe's three-pore model of peritoneal membrane permeability describes three distinct functional pore sizes: ultrasmall transcellular aquaporin-1 pores, small interendothelial pores mediating small-solute diffusion, and large venular pores mediating macromolecular protein leak.

rows: Solute-free water transport (50% of dwell ultrafiltration)
Diffusive and convective transport of small solutes
Transudation of serum albumin and macromolecules

steps.tx: The standard **Peritoneal Equilibration Test** (**PET**) stratifies peritoneal membrane transport characteristics using a **4**-hour **2.27%** dextrose dwell into four validated transport categories based on the **dialysate-to-plasma creatinine ratio**: **high** (> **0.81**), **high-average** (**0.65** to 0.81), low-average (0.50 to 0.64), and **low** (< **0.50**).
steps.say: The standard Peritoneal Equilibration Test stratifies peritoneal membrane transport characteristics using a 4-hour 2.27% dextrose dwell into four validated transport categories based on the dialysate-to-plasma creatinine ratio: high above 0.81, high-average 0.65 to 0.81, low-average 0.50 to 0.64, and low below 0.50.

steps.tx: Patients exhibiting a **high peritoneal transporter** phenotype rapidly dissipate the transperitoneal osmotic glucose gradient, resulting in premature fluid reabsorption and poor ultrafiltration on continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis (**CAPD**). These individuals achieve optimal ultrafiltration using **automated peritoneal dialysis** (**APD**) featuring rapid nocturnal cycles and long daytime **icodextrin** dwells.

These individuals achieve optimal ultrafiltration using automated peritoneal dialysis featuring rapid nocturnal cycles and long daytime icodextrin dwells.

left.title: High Transporters
points: Early loss of osmotic ultrafiltration gradient
Prone to daytime fluid retention on CAPD

right.title: Low Transporters
points: Requires higher fill volumes for clearance

steps.tx: The high-molecular-weight glucose polymer **Icodextrin** (molecular weight **13,000** to **19,000** Da) generates sustained **colloid osmosis** across small interendothelial pores during extended daytime or overnight dwells. Because icodextrin is absorbed slowly via lymphatic channels, it maintains steady ultrafiltration without hyperglycemic spikes or metabolic **ultrafiltration failure**.

steps.tx: Contemporary international **ISPD guideline adequacy** recommendations prioritize holistic clinical symptom control, maintenance of euvolemia, and nutritional status over rigid numerical clearance metrics. While historically targeting a **total Kt/V** >= **1.7** per week, modern guidelines emphasize preservation of residual renal function and individualized fluid management.

While historically targeting a total Kt/V of 1.7 or more per week, modern guidelines emphasize preservation of residual renal function and individualized fluid management.

left.title: Modern Holistic Paradigm
points: Strict euvolemia and blood pressure control

right.title: Historical Numerical Target
points: Rigid total Kt/V target >= 1.7 per week
Neglect of clinical fluid overload status

steps.tx: The diagnostic criteria for **peritoneal dialysis peritonitis** require at least two of the following: clinical symptoms of peritonitis (abdominal pain or cloudy effluent); dialysate effluent leukocyte count > **100** white blood cells/mcL with >= **50%** polymorphonuclear neutrophils (**PMNs**); and positive dialysate effluent microbiological culture.
steps.say: The diagnostic criteria for peritoneal dialysis peritonitis require at least two of the following: clinical symptoms of peritonitis such as abdominal pain or cloudy effluent; dialysate effluent leukocyte count greater than 100 white blood cells per microliter with 50% or more polymorphonuclear neutrophils; and positive dialysate effluent microbiological culture.

rows: Abdominal pain, rebound, or cloudy effluent
Gram stain or positive automated culture

steps.tx: Empirical antimicrobial therapy for suspected PD peritonitis must cover both Gram-positive and Gram-negative organisms simultaneously via **intraperitoneal** administration. Standard empirical regimens combine a first-generation cephalosporin (such as **cefazolin**) or vancomycin together with a third-generation cephalosporin (such as **ceftazidime**) or an aminoglycoside.

steps.tx: Catastrophic **Encapsulating peritoneal sclerosis** (**EPS**) is an uncommon, life-threatening complication associated with prolonged peritoneal dialysis duration (typically exceeding **5** years) and recurrent severe peritonitis. A dense **fibrocollagenous cocoon** encases the small bowel, producing severe recurrent mechanical bowel obstruction, weight loss, and catastrophic ultrafiltration failure.
